key_insight: Vega trains a vision–language–action policy that directly maps natural-language driving instructions and visual scenes to driving trajectories, enabling personalized, instruction-following behavior rather than just scene description.
problem_solved: Existing driving pipelines use language for description or reasoning but cannot flexibly follow diverse user instructions or produce personalized driving behaviors; Vega addresses this gap by grounding instructions into actionable driving policies.
method: Constructed InstructScene: a large-scale dataset (~100,000 scenes) of driving observations paired with diverse natural-language instructions and corresponding trajectories.
Train a multimodal, instruction-conditioned driving policy that fuses visual inputs and language prompts to predict trajectories or low-level controls.
Align language and action via supervised instruction–trajectory learning and modular grounding to ensure instructions map to appropriate maneuvers and constraints.
impact: Enables more natural human–vehicle interaction and personalized autonomy by letting users specify high-level or preference-based driving instructions; provides a large benchmark and modeling recipe for follow-up research in instruction-conditioned driving.

paper_title: Vega: Learning to Drive with Natural Language Instructions
paper_authors: Sicheng Zuo, Yuxuan Li, Wenzhao Zheng, Zheng Zhu, Jie Zhou
